title: Rudy Giuliani awarded Presidential Medal of Freedom a year after being pardoned for potential crimes

Rudolph Giuliani, the former New York City mayor and longtime ally of President Donald Trump, was honoured on Tuesday with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, which comes after several years of personal legal peril.
Giuliani saw criminal cases fall apart but was disbarred, found liable for defamation of election workers
Rudolph Giuliani, the former New York City mayor and longtime ally of President Donald Trump, was honoured on Tuesday with the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
The ceremony at the White House for the highest civilian honour in the U.S. was closed to the press.

In a statement, Giuliani, 82, said, "I share the credit with all the men and women who worked with me, disagreed with me and loved me — particularly those who lost their lives in the causes we undertook together."
The origins of the Medal of Freedom date back to 1945, although for nearly two decades it was awarded to those who distinguished themselves in war or the security of the U.S.

President John F. Kennedy expanded the parameters of the award, months before his 1963 death, to include civilian life, with the intent that the award would expand to include those whose lives and careers included significant achievements in the arts, public service, science or other fields.

Some 675 people have received the medal, about 12 per cent of them posthumously. Recipients need not be American — three popes, Mother Theresa, Nelson Mandela and Canadians Michael J. Fox, Frank Gehry and Edgar Bronfman Sr. are among the dozens of recipients who were born outside of the U.S.

items: Michael J. Fox among Presidential Medal of Freedom recipients

blocks.text: A former federal prosecutor, Giuliani was credited with a number of convictions of organized crime and white collar criminals.

He was a two-time New York City mayor in the final months of his tenure when commercial airliners were hijacked by Islamist militants and flown into the two World Trade Center skyscrapers on Sept. 11, 2001.

Three months later, he was named person of the year by Time magazine, which praised him for "not shrinking from the pain all around him." Giuliani was steadfast in maintaining the city would recover and rebuild, and he attended numerous funerals of the more than 2,700 people who were killed in Manhattan that day.
New York Democrat slams honour

Giuliani's selection in 2026, however, comes after a period of personal legal peril few, if any, recipients have faced. There is no record of any person ever getting a pardon for potential crimes and then later receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

As one of Trump's personal lawyers in his first term as president, Giuliani was a central figure in the false claims that the 2020 election was stolen from Trump. Giuliani tried to make the case in state legislature sessions and at more than one memorable news conference.

items: Trump pardons Rudy Giuliani, others who backed efforts to overturn 2020 election, official says

blocks.text: Giuliani also spoke at the Stop the Steal Rally on Jan. 6, 2021, in D.C., urging "trial by combat" just a couple hours before masses attacked the U.S. Capitol.

Giuliani was later indicted in Georgia for efforts to overturn that state's 2020 election result and was named an unindicted co-conspirator in a federal indictment of Trump. Both indictments fell away, the first amid a flurry of legal arguments, and the second essentially voided when Trump won the 2024 presidential election.

Both Trump and Giuliani also spread misinformation about two Georgia election workers in 2020, though it was only the former mayor who faced a civil lawsuit, with the two women awarded $146 million US after a defamation trial.

Giuliani's 2020 efforts saw him disbarred in New York state and the District of Columbia. Officials in New York said Giuliani "flagrantly misused his prominent position" and "repeatedly and intentionally made false statements, some of which were perjurious."

Democratic Rep. Jerry Nadler of New York condemned Giuliani's honour on Tuesday, highlighting his 2020 activities as well as criticisms that he downplayed the health risks and the need for masks and respirators for first responders and others at Ground Zero, the site of the 9/11 wreckage.
Health experts say the toxic stew in the air was associated with a higher incidence of certain cancers than in the general population.

"As Mayor of New York City after the terror attacks on 9/11, Rudy Giuliani lied to victims and the world about the health dangers from the toxins in the air — exacerbating the suffering of Lower Manhattan residents and heroes," said Nadler.
Trump last year pardoned Giuliani for any potential crimes, though presidential pardons don't apply to state charges.

Giuliani, who along with Trump pressured the former Arizona House Speaker to overturn Joe Biden's 2020 win in the state, was among 18 indicted in a first attempt to hold individuals criminally responsible. While that attempt was eventually dismissed by the state's Supreme Court this year, the attorney general — who was re-elected earlier this month — vowed to try again and has not publicly affirmed the case is closed.
Trump has awarded far fewer medals than other presidents, at just over 30, with about half of them from the world of sports.

Donald Trump awards the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the highest civilian honour in the U.S., to former college football coach Lou Holtz at the White House on Dec. 3, 2020. (Evan Vucci/The Associated Press)

Barack Obama presented more medals than any president, with 118. While some of his choices were criticized, he also reached across the aisle, presenting the medal to Republican politicians Jack Kemp and Richard Lugar, as well as conservative jurist Sandra Day O'Connor.

When asked in 2015, Obama said there was "no precedent for revoking the medal." The question came up in light of the sexual assault allegations faced by comedian Bill Cosby, who was awarded the Medal of Freedom in 2002 by president George W. Bush, before the allegations came to light.

A few other recipients have run afoul of the law after being honoured. They include former secretary of defence Clark Clifford, who was indicted for fraud by a grand jury over two decades after his 1969 honour, and 1987 recipient Caspar Weinberger, also a former secretary of defence, who was indicted for offences related to the Iran-Contra scandal.
Clifford, 86 when indicted, was ultimately never tried, while Weinberger was pardoned by president George H. W. Bush before his case came up for trial.

Every man who served as president between 1960 and 2000 has received the medal of freedom, with the exception of Richard Nixon, who resigned in disgrace. That list of recipients includes Bill Clinton, who struck a deal upon leaving office to avoid criminal indictment and also reached a high six-figure civil settlement with Paula Jones, who alleged sexual harassment.
